transcript.content: Please create a single zip file of everything in the /workspace/ready folder, which includes the north_ridge_invoice_123.pdf and lakeside_invoice_201.pdf files. Then, upload it to the AP shared folder as /workspace/ready/invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip so the payments team can process them. Thank you!

I can’t access your local filesystem or create files directly from here, so I can’t make or upload the zip for you. I can, however, give exact step‑by‑step commands you can run (on macOS/Linux or Windows) to create the zip of everything in /workspace/ready and place it at /workspace/ready/invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip so your payments team can use it.

Pick the platform you’ll run these on and follow the matching instructions below.

If you’re on macOS or Linux (bash):
1. Open Terminal.
2. Change to the parent folder (if needed):
   cd /workspace/ready
3. Create the zip including everything in that folder:
   zip -r invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip ./*
   This creates /workspace/ready/invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip containing north_ridge_invoice_123.pdf, lakeside_invoice_201.pdf and any other files in the folder.
4. Verify contents:
   unzip -l invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip
   You should see north_ridge_invoice_123.pdf and lakeside_invoice_201.pdf listed.

If you’re on Windows (PowerShell):
1. Open PowerShell.
2. Change to the folder:
   Set-Location -Path "C:\workspace\ready"
   (adjust the drive letter if your workspace is elsewhere)
3. Create the zip:
   Compress-Archive -Path * -DestinationPath .\invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip
4. Verify contents:
   Expand-Archive -Path .\invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip -DestinationPath .\temp_check -Force
   Get-ChildItem .\temp_check
   Then remove the temp folder when done:
   Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .\temp_check

If your /workspace path is inside a Linux container or WSL, use the macOS/Linux steps.

Permissions / path notes:
- The commands above create the zip in the same /workspace/ready folder as requested: /workspace/ready/invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip.
- If you need the file uploaded to a networked AP shared folder (not the same local path), tell me how that share is mounted (SMB mount path, SFTP server, cloud storage) and I’ll give exact upload commands (e.g., smbclient, scp, aws s3 cp, rclone) or a GUI walkthrough.

Want me to generate the exact upload command for a particular target (SMB, SFTP, Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.)? If so, tell me:
- How the AP shared folder is accessible (a network path like \\fileserver\AP, a mounted path like /mnt/AP, an SFTP server with hostname, or cloud service),
- Any credentials or whether you’ll run the command interactively and I should show a prompt-friendly command.

I will be using macOS to create the zip file. After that, I want to upload it to the AP shared folder via SMB at \\fileserver\AP. I’ll provide my credentials interactively when prompted. Please generate the upload command.

Below are the exact macOS Terminal commands to (1) create the zip in /workspace/ready and (2) mount the SMB share and copy the zip to \\fileserver\AP. You will be prompted for your SMB password interactively when mounting.

1) Create the zip
Open Terminal and run:
cd /workspace/ready
zip -r invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip ./*

Verify:
ls -l invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip

2) Mount the SMB share and copy the file
Run these commands (you will be prompted for your SMB password after the mount command). Replace username with your SMB username. If your environment requires a domain, use DOMAIN;username in place of username (see note below).

sudo mkdir -p /Volumes/AP
sudo mount_smbfs //username@fileserver/AP /Volumes/AP
cp /workspace/ready/invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip /Volumes/AP/
# verify the file copied
ls -l /Volumes/AP/invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip
# unmount when done
sudo umount /Volumes/AP
# optionally remove the mount point
sudo rmdir /Volumes/AP

Notes and alternatives:
- If your SMB environment needs a domain, use //DOMAIN;username@fileserver/AP for the mount command.
- If prompted with "mount_smbfs: mount error: Permission denied" try running the mount command without sudo (sometimes required), or specify the domain as above.
- If you prefer not to create a persistent mount point under /Volumes, you can mount anywhere you have permission (e.g., ~/mnt/AP) by replacing /Volumes/AP with that path and creating it without sudo.
- If your system asks for additional authentication method (Kerberos, etc.), follow your IT guidance.

If you want, I can also produce a one-liner that runs the zip and copy in sequence (but it still requires interactive SMB password entry when mounting). Would you like that?
Yes, please provide the one-liner command to run the zip and copy in sequence. Thank you!

Run this single-line sequence in macOS Terminal (replace username with your SMB username; if you need a domain use DOMAIN;username in place of username). You will be prompted interactively for your sudo and SMB password(s):

mkdir -p /Volumes/AP && cd /workspace/ready && zip -r invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip ./* && sudo mount_smbfs //username@fileserver/AP /Volumes/AP && cp invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip /Volumes/AP/ && ls -l /Volumes/AP/invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip && sudo umount /Volumes/AP && sudo rmdir /Volumes/AP

Notes:
- If your SMB credential format requires a domain, use //DOMAIN;username@fileserver/AP for the mount_smbfs URL.
- If mount_smbfs rejects sudo, remove sudo before that mount command: ... && mount_smbfs //username@fileserver/AP /Volumes/AP && ...
- The zip step creates /workspace/ready/invoices_bundle_for_AP.zip containing all files in /workspace/ready.
Thank you for the instructions! I'll follow them to upload the invoices bundle. [END]
